items.mnemonic_text: Toddlers Always Initiate Insane Interrogations In Grandma's Igloo: Trust vs Mistrust, Autonomy vs Shame/Doubt, Initiative vs Guilt, Industry vs Inferiority, Identity vs Role Confusion, Intimacy vs Isolation, Generativity vs Stagnation, Integrity vs Despair.
items.funny_version: Tipsy Aunties Invite Interns In; It Gets Insane. T-A-I-I-I-I-G-I: the family reunion runs from 'can I trust you?' to 'I regret nothing.'
items.explanation: The first letters run T-A-I-I-I-I-G-I, the exact order of the eight crises from infancy to old age. The four I's in a row are the trap: Initiative (preschool play), Industry (school), Identity (teens), Intimacy (young-adult dating).
items.doodle_prompt: Cartoon family reunion in an igloo: a baby hugging a blanket, a toddler on a potty, a teen in a mirror, a grandma at the end looking back at a photo album with a satisfied smile.

items.mnemonic_text: Old Age Pensioners Love Grapes: Oral, Anal, Phallic, Latency, Genital.
items.funny_version: Only Awkward People Like Grandpa's jokes: Oral (bites everything), Anal (potty boss), Phallic (Oedipus drama), Latency (cooties era), Genital (puberty hits).
items.explanation: The five first letters O-A-P-L-G give the stages in order from birth to puberty. Fixation at a stage is tested as adult traits (oral = smoking, anal = neat freak).
items.doodle_prompt: Five cartoon panels: baby chewing a phone, toddler proudly on a throne-shaped potty, kid with a crown glaring at dad, kid hiding from cooties, teen with a pimple and a crush.

items.concept: Type I vs Type II error
items.mnemonic_text: Type I = false positive (reject a true null); Type II = false negative (miss a real effect).
items.funny_version: Type I: telling a man he's pregnant. Type II: telling a very pregnant woman she's not.
items.explanation: The classic image makes the direction impossible to forget. Alpha is the Type I rate; power = 1 minus the Type II rate.
items.doodle_prompt: A doctor holding a positive pregnancy test toward a confused man, and another doctor shaking his head at a woman in labor.

items.mnemonic_text: The hypothalamus runs the 4 F's: Feeding, Fighting, Fleeing, and... Mating.
items.funny_version: Feeding, Fighting, Fleeing, and the fourth F that your biology teacher always blushed at (it's mating).
items.explanation: The joke makes the hypothalamus's drives unforgettable: hunger, aggression, fear responses and sexual behavior. It also controls the pituitary and body temperature.
items.doodle_prompt: A tiny cartoon hypothalamus at a control desk with four big buttons: a burger, boxing glove, running shoe, and a heart.

items.mnemonic_text: Positive = Plus (add something), Negative = Nix (take something away); Reinforcement = more behavior, Punishment = less behavior.
items.funny_version: The car beep stops when you buckle up: that's NEGATIVE REINFORCEMENT, not punishment. Say it louder for the people in the back.
items.explanation: Decide two things separately: was something added or removed, and did the behavior go up or down. Negative reinforcement is the most-missed cell because 'negative' sounds bad.
items.doodle_prompt: 2x2 grid of cartoon panels: dog gets treat (+R), seatbelt beep stops (-R), kid gets extra chores (+P), teen loses phone (-P).

Fundamental attribution error vs actor-observer bias

items.mnemonic_text: Can I Keep Selling Substances For Money, Officer? Citrate, Isocitrate, α-Ketoglutarate, Succinyl-CoA, Succinate, Fumarate, Malate, Oxaloacetate.
items.funny_version: Can I Keep Selling Sex For Money, Officer? Eight words, eight intermediates, one very awkward traffic stop.
items.explanation: The eight first letters follow the cycle in order starting from citrate (made from acetyl-CoA + oxaloacetate). Ending on Officer/Oxaloacetate reminds you the cycle closes where it starts.
items.doodle_prompt: A cartoon mitochondrion pulled over by a police officer, rolling down its window with a nervous smile, a circular road behind it marked with 8 stops.

items.mnemonic_text: GAV LIMP From Water: Gly, Ala, Val, Leu, Ile, Met, Pro, Phe, Trp.
items.funny_version: Gav goes LIMP From Water, like a cat in a bath. Hydrophobic side chains hide in the protein core.
items.explanation: The letters spell the nonpolar set (G, A, V, L, I, M, P, F, W), and 'from water' cues hydrophobic. They cluster in the interior of globular proteins and in membrane-spanning helices.
items.doodle_prompt: A cartoon guy named Gav going floppy as he's lowered into a bathtub, with nine amino acid side chains clinging to a dry island.

items.mnemonic_text: Try Pulling My Aorta: Tricuspid, Pulmonary, Mitral, Aortic.
items.funny_version: Toilet Paper My Ass: the valve order every med student remembers and no one admits learning.
items.explanation: The four valves in the path of blood: right AV, right semilunar, left AV, left semilunar.
items.doodle_prompt: A cartoon heart with four doors in order, with a toilet paper roll unrolling through them.

items.mnemonic_text: GFR = Salt, Sugar, Sex: Glomerulosa (aldosterone), Fasciculata (cortisol), Reticularis (androgens).
items.funny_version: Salt, Sugar, Sex: the deeper you go, the sweeter it gets.
items.explanation: Layers outside to inside match mineralocorticoids, glucocorticoids, then androgens. GFR also matches the kidney's filtration acronym for extra stickiness.
items.doodle_prompt: A cartoon adrenal gland as a three-layer cake with a salt shaker, a sugar cube, and a heart on each layer.

items.mnemonic_text: Goodness Gracious, Father Franklin Did Go By Picking Pumpkins (to) Prepare Pies: Glucose, G6P, F6P, F-1,6-BP, DHAP, G3P, 1,3-BPG, 3-PG, 2-PG, PEP, Pyruvate.
items.funny_version: Good Girls Flirt For Drinks; Guys Buy Pricey Pints, Pass-out Promptly. Glycolysis: ten steps from sugar to the floor.
items.explanation: Each capital letter is one intermediate in order; DHAP and G3P are the two halves from aldolase. Pyruvate last is where the party (and the anaerobic hangover, lactate) begins.
items.doodle_prompt: Cartoon Ben Franklin picking pumpkins along a winding 10-step path that ends at a pumpkin pie labeled PYRUVATE.

items.concept: Fatty acid synthesis vs β-oxidation location

items.mnemonic_text: OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain (of electrons).
items.funny_version: LEO the lion says GER: Lose Electrons Oxidized, Gain Electrons Reduced. LEO is a lion who's lost everything and still roars.
items.explanation: Both phrases lock in that oxidation means losing electrons (oxidation number goes up) and reduction means gaining them. The reducing agent is the one that gets oxidized.
items.doodle_prompt: A cartoon lion on an oil rig dropping electrons into the sea while a second lion catches them in a net.

items.mnemonic_text: AN OX and a RED CAT: Anode = Oxidation, Reduction = Cathode.
items.funny_version: AN OX and a RED CAT walk into an electrochemical cell. The ox loses electrons (anode), the cat gains them (cathode). Electrons flow from the ox to the cat: A to C, alphabetical.
items.explanation: True for every cell, galvanic or electrolytic. Electrons always travel anode → cathode through the wire.
items.doodle_prompt: A cartoon ox at the left electrode and a red cat at the right, with electrons hopping along a wire from ox to cat.

items.mnemonic_text: So I Brought No Clean Clothes: H2SO4, HI, HBr, HNO3, HCl, HClO4.
items.funny_version: So I Brought No Clean Clothes... for the sleepover. Strong acids dissociate completely, no regrets.
items.explanation: Six common strong acids; everything else on the MCAT is weak unless stated. HF is a trap: weak.
items.doodle_prompt: A cartoon student with an empty suitcase at a sleepover, holding six acid bottles instead of clothes.

items.mnemonic_text: H-bonds are FON: H must bond to F, O, or N.
items.funny_version: Hydrogen only flirts with FON: F, O, N. Everybody else gets left on read.
items.explanation: H-bonding needs H attached to a highly electronegative small atom and a lone pair on another. That raises boiling points dramatically (water vs H2S).
items.doodle_prompt: A cartoon hydrogen at a party only talking to F, O and N, ignoring C and S in the corner.

items.mnemonic_text: SN2 = 2 molecules in rate law, 1 step, backside attack, inversion, 1° substrate. SN1 = 1 molecule in rate law, 2 steps, carbocation, racemic, 3° substrate.
items.funny_version: SN2 is a backstabber: attacks from behind and flips you inside out. SN1 waits for the leaving group to dump you first, then anyone can hook up from either side.
items.explanation: The number in the name is the molecularity of the rate law, opposite to the number of steps. Polar aprotic solvents favor SN2; polar protic favor SN1.
items.doodle_prompt: A cartoon nucleophile sneaking up behind a carbon with an umbrella flipping inside out, next to a lonely carbocation surrounded by suitors.

items.concept: Fischer projection: D vs L sugars

items.mnemonic_text: Raging Martians Invaded Venus Using X-ray Guns: Radio, Microwave, Infrared, Visible, Ultraviolet, X-ray, Gamma.
items.funny_version: Rich Men In Vegas Use eXpensive Gadgets. Frequency and energy go up, wavelength goes down, and so does your bank balance.
items.explanation: The seven first letters give the order of increasing frequency and photon energy (E = hf), and decreasing wavelength.
items.doodle_prompt: Cartoon Martians on Venus firing seven ray guns of increasing wiggliness, from a lazy radio wave to a tight gamma zigzag.

items.mnemonic_text: 1st = Lazy (inertia), 2nd = Math (F = ma), 3rd = Revenge (equal and opposite).
items.funny_version: Newton's 1st: your couch potato roommate. 2nd: F = ma, the only math. 3rd: push me and I push you back.
items.explanation: One word per law gives its meaning. Third-law pairs act on different objects, so they never cancel.
items.doodle_prompt: Three cartoon panels: a sloth on a couch, a calculator, a kid shoving a wall and sliding backward.

items.mnemonic_text: Approaching = higher frequency; receding = lower frequency.
items.funny_version: The ambulance siren: 'neee-' as it rushes at you, '-owww' as it leaves, like your crush walking past.
items.explanation: Relative motion compresses or stretches the waves you receive. Source and observer approaching both raise the observed frequency.
items.doodle_prompt: A cartoon ambulance with tight sound waves in front and stretched waves behind.

items.mnemonic_text: Flow ∝ r⁴: double the radius, 16× the flow.
items.funny_version: Blood vessels are drama queens: shrink the radius by half and flow drops to 1/16.
items.explanation: Q = πr⁴ΔP / 8ηL. The fourth power explains why small vasoconstriction changes blood flow so much.
items.doodle_prompt: A cartoon blood vessel fainting dramatically as it narrows, with a tiny trickle of blood.

items.mnemonic_text: V = IR: 'Victoria Is Royal.'
items.funny_version: Voltage is the pressure, current is the flow, resistance is the drama blocking the hallway.
items.explanation: Cover the one you want in a V-over-I×R triangle. Power: P = IV = I²R = V²/R.
items.doodle_prompt: A cartoon queen Victoria on a throne pushing water through a pipe with a narrow drama-filled section.
